context.situation: I chair the national response committee. A novel respiratory pathogen has been confirmed in our largest port city. Case numbers are low but doubling roughly weekly. Modelling is highly uncertain and the modellers disagree with each other. Restricting movement would impose severe and immediate economic damage, and our tourism and freight sectors are already fragile. There is no confirmed community transmission outside the port city. My instinct is to wait a further two weeks for better data, since acting on uncertain modelling and being wrong would be its own catastrophe.
context.whatMatters: Avoiding unnecessary economic damage while protecting public health.
context.stakeholders: Public, businesses, health service, care homes, government.
context.uncertainties: True transmission rate and extent of community spread.

evidence.text: Confirmed cases are doubling approximately weekly.
Modellers disagree substantially on the transmission rate.
No community transmission confirmed outside the port city.
Testing capacity is limited; we are testing symptomatic arrivals only.
Business groups warn restrictions would be severely damaging.
Acting early on uncertain data risks being visibly wrong.
Care homes have raised staffing and equipment concerns.
